subject.title: fix(cli-runner): sweep orphaned bundle MCP temp dirs at gateway startup

question: Is the Linux real-host proof plus fail-closed behavior sufficient to accept the residual process-visibility risk on other supported platforms?
rationale: Correct orphan classification depends on platform process inventory, and unit tests cannot prove that Windows PowerShell or other POSIX environments expose every relevant live child command line.

options.title: Accept conservative liveness sweep
options.body: Merge with the current fail-closed design because false positives retain directories, empty scans retain everything, and the Linux production path has positive exact-head proof.

options.title: Require broader platform proof
options.body: Hold merge until a Windows or additional POSIX real-host run demonstrates orphan removal and preservation of a live referenced directory.

recommendation.title: Accept conservative liveness sweep
recommendation.body: Merge with the current fail-closed design because false positives retain directories, empty scans retain everything, and the Linux production path has positive exact-head proof.
